n.story:
Your role is transitioning from a manual laborer to a 'smart city' technician. While the physical act of clearing debris remains central, the way you navigate your day is now dictated by high-precision algorithms. Instead of following a static route, you are guided by real-time data that identifies high-litter areas based on foot traffic patterns, weather events, and IoT sensor alerts from 'smart' bins. You spend less time driving aimlessly and more time addressing specific urban hygiene challenges that machines cannot yet master.

As autonomous sweeping vehicles become more common, your responsibilities shift toward oversight and specialized intervention. You handle the complex 'edge cases'—clearing blocked drains, disinfecting irregular public furniture, and managing hazardous waste—while your AI-augmented equipment handles the long, repetitive stretches of pavement. You are the human troubleshooter in an increasingly automated urban maintenance ecosystem, ensuring that safety protocols are met in unpredictable pedestrian environments where sensors might fail.
auto: Operating mechanical sweepers on standard roads
Monitoring waste levels in public bins
Basic surface disinfection in open areas
amp: Complex obstacle navigation in high-traffic zones
n.adv: Focus on gaining basic technical literacy with IoT devices and autonomous machinery. Your value will shift from pure physical labor to the ability to manage and troubleshoot the smart tools that keep cities clean.
